post.description:
Import a transcript into a namespace (editors; admins may name a new namespace). The namespace's pipeline, or
the one chosen (`pipeline`), is queued as a job.

Capture a web page as a document (editors; admins may name a new namespace): the namespace's pipeline, or
`pipeline`, keeps the page as it is now, as a PDF (a link to a PDF is kept as it is; other pages are printed by
headless Chromium), and reads it page by page. Only public addresses on ports 80 and 443 can be captured (and the
networks in documents.web_networks). Audited as `import.web`.

Import a video or podcast episode by its address (editors; admins may name a new namespace), when
documents.video_urls lets it (off by default): its transcribe step downloads the media with yt-dlp, one video, never
a playlist, through the same checks as capturing a web page (public addresses on ports 80 and 443, and the
networks in documents.web_networks), at most uploads.max_mb; then it's transcribed like an upload. Audited as
`import.video`.

Capture one or many web pages at once (editors; admins may name a new namespace): pasted addresses, one per
line, a JSON list of them (`urls`), or a file: a list of addresses, a browser's bookmark export (HTML) or Chrome's Bookmarks file (JSON). Each link becomes
a page captured as a document, as `POST /import/web` does, tagged with the bookmark folders it was in
(`folders_as_tags`). At most 500 links; a link already captured in the namespace isn't captured again, and one that
can't be is skipped, saying why. Audited as `import.web` once, with how many were queued.
Parse without saving: what the importer would make of this text or file.

Import chosen files of a storage source into a namespace now, rather than watching their folder (admins, like
sources; a new namespace is created). Audio, video, documents (PDFs) and images stay on the source and run the
namespace's pipeline, or `pipeline`; transcripts are imported, and PDFs, Word and text files too with
`documents_as: transcript`. Each file
gets a result: queued, already (the namespace has it from this source), skipped (not audio, video, a document, an
image or a transcript) or error. Audited as `import.source`.

post.description:
Ask a question, optionally from a page (`context`: the page, its text and any highlighted part, which the model
reads with the question). Streams events: step, approval, notice, passages, token (answer text), error, stopped (POST
/chats/{cid}/stop: what came before is saved, marked stopped), meta (the answer's record, kept with it: what produced
it), done (the saved message id).

A conversation is a tree of versions (GET /chats/{cid}: `tree`, and each message's `versions`); the question goes
on from `parent` when given (any message of the conversation), else from the version showing (`head`). With
`regenerate` (an answer's id) its question is answered again, as a new version beside that answer (`content` isn't
needed; `model` may pick another). With `edit`, one of your earlier questions is edited: this question becomes a new
version beside it and is answered, and the old one stays with what followed it (404 if it isn't a question in this
conversation). Either keeps the page the question was asked from (where, and the highlighted text; not the page's
text, which isn't kept) unless `context` is given, and streams `branch` first ({message, parent, versions}: the
new version, the message it follows and its versions); so does a question beside others under `parent`.

`/clear` makes the model start afresh (the messages stay to read) and `/compact [what to keep]` folds the
conversation so far into its summary now; each streams cleared or compacted, then its reply as an answer.
